Investigative Journalist Kate McClymont Testifies in Alan Jones Indecent Assault Trial

03 Nov 2026, 07:05 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

2 min read

Key takeawaysAward-winning investigative journalist Kate McClymont has provided evidence in the Sydney trial of former radio broadcaster Alan Jones. Jones has pleaded not guilty to 21 charges involving allegations of indecent assault and sexual touching against five men.

Investigative Reporting in Court

Award-winning investigative journalist Kate McClymont has provided evidence in the Sydney trial of former radio broadcaster Alan Jones. Jones has pleaded not guilty to 21 charges involving allegations of indecent assault and sexual touching against five men.

Testifying at the Downing Centre local court on Tuesday, McClymont stated that the alleged victims she interviewed received no financial benefit or other incentives from her or her media employer for sharing their accounts. Her published reporting in late 2023 preceded further individuals coming forward and the subsequent establishment of New South Wales police Strike Force Bonnefin.

Testimony and Cross-Examination Highlights

Key details emerged during the proceedings regarding journalistic processes and police involvement:

  • Editorial Practice: McClymont told prosecutor Georgina Wright that she consistently sought comment from Jones and his legal representatives via text and email prior to publication.
  • Confidentiality: She confirmed speaking to three alleged victims while keeping their individual stories confidential from one another.
  • Subpoenaed Materials: The court heard that McClymont did not initially provide interview notes or recordings to police due to confidentiality, but later received and complied with a subpoena for the material in 2026.
  • Cross-Examination: Under questioning from defence barrister Gabrielle Bashir SC, McClymont rejected the suggestion that readership and advertising metrics influenced her work, stating such metrics were irrelevant to her role as a journalist.

Background and Context

Jones concluded his prominent radio career following on-air incidents in 2020 that impacted his former station's advertising revenue. Police arrested him at his Sydney apartment in late 2024 following an investigation conducted by Strike Force Bonnefin. The ongoing hearing is presided over by Judge Glenn Walsh.

Practical Implications and Verification

Observers and interested members of the public seeking to verify details of ongoing court proceedings can consult official New South Wales court lists and authorized legal reporting from accredited media outlets covering the Downing Centre local court.
